We developed Lunar Landing Site Navigator, a web application that helps mission planners compare lunar south pole landing sites and select optimal launch windows. Powered by authentic NASA data (LRO LOLA topography, JPL Horizons, and PGDA illumination maps), the platform evaluates seven candidate regions in interactive 3D and 2D views.

details:
We developed Lunar Landing Site Navigator, an interactive 3D and 2D web application designed to compare lunar south pole landing sites and identify optimal mission dates. Built for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge, our tool integrates real NASA datasets—including LRO LOLA elevation models, JPL Horizons ephemerides, and PGDA illumination maps—across seven official candidate regions.

The app addresses the challenge by calculating Sun and Earth visibility against each site’s actual local terrain horizon, rather than an idealized flat horizon. Users can explore the south pole in 3D, scrub through time, compare sites side-by-side, inspect 360° horizon panoramas, toggle terrain layers (slope, permanent shadows, illumination), and receive mission-tailored site recommendations.

This is critical for Artemis-era exploration because assuming a flat horizon makes all polar sites appear nearly identical (~51% sunlight), whereas real topography dramatically alters illumination from 40% to 84%. By revealing how terrain dictates power, communications, and safety, our tool enables smarter, data-driven mission planning.
